patterns.regex: protected branch|branch [^\n]* is protected|pre-receive hook declined
patterns.title: push to a protected branch
patterns.explain: main is protected: nobody pushes to it directly, on purpose. Changes reach it through a pull request.
patterns.fix: Put your commit on a branch (git switch -c my-branch; git push -u origin my-branch) and open a pull request. If you committed on main by mistake, git reset --hard origin/main after moving the commit to a branch.

patterns.title: push rejected: the remote has commits you don't
patterns.explain: Someone pushed to that branch since you last pulled, so git refuses to overwrite their work.
patterns.fix: git pull (it brings their commits in; fix any conflict), then push again. Never force-push to get past this on a shared branch.

patterns.title: no upstream branch
patterns.explain: The branch exists only on your machine; git doesn't know where to push it yet.
patterns.fix: Run the command git suggests: git push -u origin <your-branch>. After that a bare git push works.

patterns.title: merge conflict
patterns.explain: Two changes touched the same lines and git can't choose for you. It marked both versions in the file.
patterns.fix: Open the file, keep what should stay, delete the <<<<<<<, ======= and >>>>>>> lines, then git add the file and git commit (git status shows where you are).

patterns.title: not in a git repository
patterns.explain: You're not inside a cloned repo, so git has nothing to work on.
patterns.fix: cd into the repo's folder first (pwd and ls show where you are), for example cd ~/lab/<repo>.

patterns.regex: would be overwritten by (checkout|merge)|Please commit your changes or stash them
patterns.title: uncommitted changes in the way
patterns.explain: You have edits that aren't committed, and this command would overwrite them.
patterns.fix: Commit them (git add, git commit), or park them with git stash and bring them back with git stash pop. git status shows what is pending.

patterns.regex: Authentication failed|could not read Username|invalid credentials|HTTP Basic: Access denied
patterns.title: git can't sign in
patterns.explain: git didn't send a valid token for the server.
patterns.fix: Your terminal normally has a token in ~/.git-credentials. If this keeps happening, tell the facilitator.

patterns.title: detached HEAD
patterns.explain: You're looking at a commit, not a branch, so new commits belong to no branch.
patterns.fix: To keep work from here: git switch -c my-branch. To go back: git switch main.

patterns.title: git can't find that name
patterns.explain: There is no branch or file by that name (check the spelling and the folder you're in).
patterns.fix: git branch -a lists branches; git status and ls show files. A new branch needs git switch -c <name> (or git checkout -b <name>).

patterns.regex: nothing added to commit|no changes added to commit|nothing to commit
patterns.title: nothing to commit
patterns.explain: Either you have no changes, or you haven't staged them (git add) before committing.
patterns.fix: git status shows modified files; git add <file> stages one; then git commit -m "...".

patterns.regex: Please tell me who you are|unable to auto-detect email
patterns.title: git doesn't know who you are
patterns.explain: git needs a name and email to sign commits.
patterns.fix: git config --global user.name "Your Name" and git config --global user.email you@example.com

patterns.title: unrelated histories
patterns.explain: The two branches share no common history, usually because the repo was started separately.
patterns.fix: Check you're pulling the right repo and branch before forcing anything; ask the facilitator.

patterns.title: command not found
patterns.explain: The shell doesn't know that command: a typo, or the tool isn't installed here.
patterns.fix: Check the spelling against the lab. Tab completion helps: type a few letters and press Tab.
